5850.html:
5850 tucchyá 'empty, vain' RV., n. 'emptiness' RV., tuccha- 'empty', n. 'trifle' BhP., °aka- lex. 2. *tuśya-. [tuśya- prob. ← Ir., cf. Khot. tuśśa-, Psht. taš < *tusya- EVP 84]
    1. Pa. tuccha-, °aka- 'empty'; Pk. tuccha-, cuccha-, chuccha- 'empty, small, light'; Gy. eur. čučo 'empty'; K. tᵃċh f. 'trifle', ċhọ̆ċᵘ 'empty, worthless'; P. tucch 'contemptible'; Ku. chūco 'light, contemptible'; N. chuco 'mean, vile'; B. chū̃c, °cā, chũcho 'mean vile rogue'; Or. tuchā, cuchā, chu° 'empty, alone'; Bhoj. chū̃ch 'empty', OAw. chūchā, lakh. chū̃ch; H. chūch, °chā 'empty, contemptible' (→ P. chūchā 'empty, vile'); Si. sis, his 'empty, useless'. — Ash. tūċ 'floor' (semant. cf. Lat. spatium > OIt. spazzo 'floor')? — H. ṭuccā 'mean, worthless' prob. belongs to the 'defective' group s.v. *ṭuṇṭa-. — See Add.
    2. Bshk. tūši 'a little' (AO xviii 254 < *tuṣya-: túṣa-); Tor. tūš 'empty', Phal. Sh.koh. tiš.
    TUJ 'push, urge': *tukṣā-, *tuñjati; *uttukta-.
    Addenda: tucchyá-: Md. hus 'empty, finished', adv. 'only, absolutely'.

10299 mr̥ṣṭá¹ 'rubbed, washed, pure' RV., 'prepared, savoury' R., 'sweet, pleasant' MBh., miṣṭa-¹ 'dainty, sweet' MBh. [√mr̥j or √mr̥ś]
    Pa. Pk. maṭṭha- 'wiped, polished, clean'; P. maṭṭhā m., °ṭhī f. 'wheaten fritter'; A. māṭhiba 'to smooth with a hammer'; Or. maṭhā 'polished', māṭhibā 'to polish'; H. maṭṭhā 'rubbed smooth', miṭhnā 'to be effaced'; M. māṭhṇẽ 'to polish'; Si. maṭa 'polished, smooth, shining'; — ext. -r- and -l-: N. muṭhārnu 'to smooth, trim (a stick)'; G. maṭhārvũ, °ṭhervũ 'to smooth', M. maṭhā̆rṇẽ, maṭhāḷṇẽ, māṭharṇẽ, māṭhaḷṇẽ 'to smooth by hammering'. — With unexpl. loss of aspiration (poss. influenced by Drav., Tam. miti 'tread on', &c. DED 3982?): Pa. maṭṭa- 'wiped, polished, pure'; Pk. miṭijjaï 'is wiped out', K. miṭun, S. miṭaṇu, P. miṭnā, ḍog. maṭanā tr. 'to wipe'; N. māṭ-meṭ 'exhaustion'; A. miṭiba 'to be settled'; B. miṭā, meṭā 'to be wiped out'; Or. miṭibā 'to be settled', tr. 'to rescind'; Mth. meṭab 'to be rubbed out' (X *vijjhāyati in mijhāeb 'to extinguish'), H. miṭnā, OMarw. miṭaï, G. miṭvũ, maṭvũ; M. miṭṇẽ tr. 'to efface'; — tr. with e: Pk. mēṭavaï 'wipes out', S. meṭaṇu, P. meṭṇā; WPah. (Joshi) meṭṇu 'to spoil'; N. meṭnu 'to wipe out', Or. meṇṭibā, OAw. meṭaï, H. meṭnā.
    Forms with -(r)i- < -r̥- were early (e.g. miṣṭa- in MBh.) specialized as 'pure, good, (esp.) sweet': Pk. miṭṭha- 'sweet'; Gy. eur. mišto 'good, right, useful'; Ash. mäistä, maiṣta 'good, sound, true', Bashg. mustā 'clever'; Tir. mᵊrəxta, (LSI) mrixt 'sweet', Woṭ. miṭh, Gaw. miṣṭa, Bshk. mīc̣h, muc̣, Tor. miṭh; Mai. miṭha 'good'; Sh. mĭṣṭŭ 'good, in good health'; K. myūṭhᵘ, f. mīṭhᷴ 'sweet', pog. miṭh 'a kiss'; S. miṭho 'sweet', miṭhī f. 'a kiss'; L. P. miṭṭhā 'sweet', WPah.bhad. miṭṭhū, paṅ. cur. miṭṭhā, (Joshi) miṭhā, Ku.gng. miṭh, N. miṭho, A. miṭhā, B. miṭha, meṭ(h)o, Or. miṭhā̆, Mth. Bhoj. mīṭh, OAw. mīṭha, H. miṭh, mīṭhā, miṭṭhā, G. mīṭhũ; M. mīṭh n. 'salt', miṭhā 'sweet'; Ko. mīṭa 'salt'.
    Addenda: mr̥ṣṭá-¹: S.kcch. miṭho 'sweet', WPah.kṭg. (kc.) míṭṭhɔ 'sweet, tasty', m. 'sweets', kṭg. məṭhέi f.; J. miṭhā 'sweet'; Garh. miṭṭhu, maṭhṇu 'to wipe off'; OMarw. sumīṭha 'very sweet'; A. miṭhā (phonet. mitha, mita) AFD 203, 206, māṭhiba 'to smooth' AFD 337, Md. mařanī 'grazes, sharpens, slices', meřum 'wounding'.
    *mēḍayati see mēlayati Add².

10729.html:
10729 riktá 'emptied' AV., riktaka- 'unladen' Mn. [~ *rikṇa-. — √ric]
    Pa. ritta-, °aka- 'empty'; Pk. ritta- 'empty', n. 'absence'; Tir. rə́tu 'empty'; Kal.rumb. ritém 'I pour into'; P. rītī 'empty', WPah.jaun. rītō, Ku. rīto, N. ritto (rittinu 'to be empty', caus. rittyāunu), H. rītā (ritā with i from intr. ritnā 'to be empty', caus. ritānā), M. ritā, Ko. rittẽ; Si. rit 'empty, emptiness'.
    Addenda: riktá-: WPah.kṭg. rittɔ 'empty', Garh. rittu (despite P. rītī, the -tt- of WPah. Garh. Ku. N. Ko. prob. is emph. doubling).

2554.html:
2554 *ōdra or *audra- 'wet'. 2. ōlla-² lex. [√ud²]
    1. Pk. odda- 'wet'; A. odā 'half dried or roasted (of grain), untempered (of metals)'; B. oda, odā 'wet, damp'; Or. oda 'wetness', odā 'wet, damp'; H. od m. 'wetness', odā 'wet'. — All poss. < ṓdman- esp. in view of the substantives of Or. H.
    2. Pk. olla- 'wet', °laï 'wets'; H. ol 'wet, damp'; M. ol n.f. 'dampness', olā 'wet, fresh, green', olaviṇẽ to 'moisten'; Ko. vallẽ 'wet'.

    Pa.     *taiktikā-; *tiktapūra-; *rājikātiktaka-.

13393.html:
13393 sicyátē 'is sprinkled' RV. [√sic]
    Pk. siccaṁta- pres. part. 'being sprinkled'; Kho. (Lor.) čičeik 'to pour from one vessel to another' (or < śucyati); A. xisiba 'to sprinkle, scatter, sow broadcast, bale', xisani 'baling scoop'; — with -jj- after act. siñj- < siñcáti: L. sijjaṇ 'to be moistened', awāṇ. sijjuṇ 'to be wet'; P. sijjṇā 'to be watered', caus. sijāuṇā (see also svidyati).
    *siñca- 'emission'. [Replaces sḗka-. — √sic]
    *niḥsiñca-.
    Addenda: sicyátē: Garh. sīcṇu 'to sprinkle' or < sin̄cáti.

13933.html:
13933 svidyati 'sweats' KātyŚr., °tē Yājñ. [√svid]
    Pa. sijjati 'sweats', Pk. sijjaï; L. sijjaṇ 'to be moistened'; P. sijjṇā 'to be wet, be soaked', kgr. sijjā 'damp' (cf. esp. sijj-pasijj jāṇā < *prasvidyati: but see sicyatē); H. sījnā 'to sweat, exude'. — In Pa. sijjati intr. 'boils', H. sījnā intr. 'to simmer (of pot on low fire)' derivation fr. svidyati is supported by svinná- 'sweating' VS. ~ 'seethed, boiled' Hariv.; but the latter meaning may be a reflection of a MIA. pp. of śrīṇā́ti and the Pa. and H. words be < *śrīyatē.

13934.html:
13934 svinná 'sweating' VS., 'seethed' Hariv. [√svid]
    Pa. sinna- 'wet with sweat, boiled'; Pk. siṇṇa- 'sweating'; K. syonᵘ 'soft, tender (of food by long cooking), dull-witted', sĕnun, sĕnnun 'to become enfeebled by excessive heat or sweat, become soft or tender by cooking (of food)', caus. sẹ̆ñĕrun 'to melt, soften (food with water or cooking)'; — (or poss. < sníh-): L. sinnā̃ 'wet', sinnhā m. 'unseasoned wood'; P. sinnhā 'wet', sinnhṇā 'to be wet'.
    SVR̥ 'sound': sura-¹, svará-, svarant-, svārá-; niḥsvara-, *nisvara-, susvara-.

13798.html:
13798 sníh f. 'wetness, moisture' TS. (snḗhiti-, snī́hiti- f. pl. 'waters' RV., snĭ̄hiti- f. 'moisture' TĀr., snīhán- m. or snīhā́- f. 'mucus of nose' ŚBr.), '*snow' R. L. Turner BSOAS xviii 447, xix 375. [√snih]

    *snihācala-.
    Addenda: sníh-: WPah.kṭg. sínnhɔ 'wet'.
